verdict.rationale: Superpowers ships a first-party writing-skills skill that 'teaches you to author and test new skills' through a documented TDD process, and a hands-on probe confirms skills are SKILL.md folders with `name` frontmatter. The evidence never quotes a fill-in template or a frontmatter specification, so how much reverse-engineering is avoided is unproven. Missing for 10: a documented SKILL.md template, an explicit name/description frontmatter schema, and independent corroboration of authoring a new skill from the docs.

support.subject: As a developer, I can author a new skill from a documented template — a SKILL.md with name and description frontmatter — without reverse-engineering existing skills

citations.quote: The writing-skills module teaches you to author and test new skills
You write test cases (pressure scenarios with subagents), watch them fail (baseline behavior), write the skill (documentation), watch tests pass (agents comply), and refactor (close loopholes).
the installed SKILL.md frontmatter (name: test-driven-development) read back cleanly
Codex, Copilot CLI, and Gemini CLI all also recognize `~/.agents/skills/` as a cross-runtime alias.
